'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Gaza peace plan]]
***The [[United States]] and the [[Israel]]-backed [[Gaza Humanitarian Foundation]] announce it will permanently wind down operations, after closing its distribution sites six weeks ago. [https://apnews.com/article/gaza-humanitarian-foundation-shuts-down-dce3d8f08c814839bdeef6aed31bfe3d (AP)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**[[2025 Federal Constabulary headquarters attack]]
***A [[Jamaat-ul-Ahrar]] [[Suicide attack|suicide bomber]] blows himself up outside the [[Federal Constabulary]] headquarters in [[Peshawar]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]], killing three people and wounding two others. Two more armed attackers attempt to enter the camp and [[Mass shooting|open fire]], wounding nine other people, before being killed in a [[shootout]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1957041/federal-constabulary-headquarters-in-peshawar-under-attack (''Dawn'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Israeli forces kill a [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] militant that killed two [[Kfir Brigade]] soldiers during a [[vehicle-ramming attack]] in May 2024 and arrest several others in [[Nablus]], [[West Bank]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-875080 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Moro conflict]]
**Seven militants, including a field commander of the [[Moro Islamic Liberation Front]] (MILF), are killed in an encounter in [[Cotabato]], [[Philippines]], involving MILF factions caught in a [[rido|clan feud]]. [https://mb.com.ph/2025/11/25/milf-commander-6-others-killed-in-north-cotabato-gun-battles (PNA via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
*[[Western DR Congo clashes]]
**At least 14 people are killed in conflict between rival ethnic militias in [[Kwamouth]], [[Mai-Ndombe Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-militia-mobondo-attack-945bf4c4ba94660b33502c95952bbd05 (AP)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**At least seven people are killed, including two attackers, and two others are injured in a [[mass shooting]] when unidentified gunmen opened fire on the governor of [[Taiz]]'s motorcade on a road linking the southwestern city to the rest of [[Yemen]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-ca/news/world/gunmen-attack-a-yemeni-official-s-motorcade-killing-5-security-officers/ar-AA1R3SSx?ocid=winp1taskbar&cvid=2a19c634191b44c7a597cf91ca618d46&ei=26 (MSN)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Seven people are killed and more than 30 others are injured after two private buses [[head-on collision|collided head-on]] in [[Tenkasi district]], [[Tamil Nadu]], [[India]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/india/bus-collision-tamil-nadu-tenkasi-death-toll-b2871108.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/seven-persons-killed-more-than-60-injured-as-two-private-buses-collide-intenkasi/article70316905.ece (''The Hindu'')]
*Five people are killed and 13 others are injured after a bus carrying pilgrims overturns and plunges into a gorge in [[Tehri Garhwal]], [[Uttarakhand]], India. [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/bus-pilgrims-falls-gorge-uttarakhand-reversing-10383548/?ref=archive_pg (''The Indian Express'')]
*Two [[Mountaineering|climber]]s are killed after falling from a [[ridge]] on [[Aoraki / Mount Cook]] in [[New Zealand]] during a guided ascent. [https://www.reuters.com/world/american-climber-among-two-dead-after-fall-new-zealands-highest-mountain-2025-11-26/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Myanmar–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] announces the end of [[temporary protected status]] for approximately 4,000 [[Myanmar]] nationals in January 2026, with the [[United States Department of Homeland Security|Department of Homeland Security]] citing changes in Myanmar's [[Politics of Myanmar|political]] and security climate, particularly [[2025–26 Myanmar general election|the upcoming election]], for the policy change. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-terminates-temporarily-legal-status-myanmar-citizens-2025-11-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]], [[War on drugs]]
**The [[United States]] formally declares [[Cartel of the Suns]], an [[Hypernymy and hyponymy|umbrella]] designation for [[National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela|Venezuelan Armed Forces]] officials allegedly involved in the [[illegal drug trade in Venezuela|drug trade]], as a [[United States Department of State list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations|Foreign Terrorist Organization]]. [https://www.kuow.org/stories/u-s-set-to-label-maduro-tied-cartel-de-los-soles-as-a-terror-organization (AP via KUOW)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Arrest of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**A panel of [[Brazil]]'s [[Supreme Federal Court]] upholds an order to keep former [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] in [[Federal Police of Brazil|police]] custody after he allegedly tampered with his [[Electronic tagging|ankle monitor]] while appealing a 27-year prison sentence for [[2022–2023 Brazilian coup plot|plotting a coup]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-top-court-panel-votes-keep-bolsonaro-under-police-custody-2025-11-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Capital punishment in Sri Lanka]]
**A [[Judiciary of Sri Lanka|court]] in [[Embilipitiya]], [[Sabaragamuwa Province]], [[Sri Lanka]], sentences ten people, including three women, [[Capital punishment|to death]] for the murder of a man in October 2011. Sri Lanka has an unofficial moratorium in place, with the last execution taking place in 1976. [https://www.onlanka.com/news/ten-people-sentenced-to-death-over-2011-embilipitiya-murder.html (''OnLanka'')] [https://www.dailymirror.lk/breaking-news/Ten-sentenced-to-death-over-murder-in-Embilipitiya/108-325886 (''Mirror Sri Lanka'')]
*[[Prosecution of James Comey]], [[Prosecution of Letitia James]]
**[[United States federal judge|Judge]] [[Cameron McGowan Currie]] rules that the appointment of [[Lindsey Halligan]] as [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia|U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia]] was illegal, dismissing the indictments against [[James Comey]] and [[Letitia James]] without [[prejudice (legal term)|prejudice]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/judge-dismisses-cases-james-comey-letitia-james-finding-prosecutor-was-rcna244775 (NBC News)]
*One person is killed and ten others are injured when a man [[vehicle-ramming attack|rammed a stolen car]] into pedestrians in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]]. The perpetrator is arrested by [[Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department|police]] at the scene. [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/japan/tokyo-car-crash-hit-and-run-b2871128.html (''The Independent'')] [https://apnews.com/article/accident-injury-police-japan-holiday-530ee11a714cdacc8c1e43a339c406c6 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Egyptian parliamentary election]]
**[[Egyptians]] vote in the second round to elect [[Parliament of Egypt|parliament]] members after the [[National Elections Authority]] annulled votes in 19 of the 70 constituencies due to various violations. [https://apnews.com/article/egypt-election-parliament-rerun-6c6e86670ff2df30596238c097659c95 (AP)]
*[[India–Israel relations]]
**The [[Israeli government]] approves a plan jointly-coordinated with the [[Indian government]] to admit 5,800 members of the [[India]]-based [[Bnei Menashe]] ethnic group to Israel under ''[[Aliyah]]'' laws and will settle them to the [[Galilee]] region. [https://www.dw.com/en/israel-to-admit-thousands-from-indias-jewish-lost-tribe/a-74855366 (DW)]
*[[Pauline Hanson's burqa incidents]]
**The [[Australia]]n [[Australian Senate|Senate]] [[censure]]s and suspends [[Queensland]] senator [[Pauline Hanson]] for a week after she wore a [[burqa]] in the chamber to push for a [[burqa ban in Australia]].  [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/australia-pauline-hanson-burqa-far-right-senator-called-racist-over-protest/ (AFP via CBS News)]
*[[List of trade unions in Belgium|Unions]] in [[Belgium]] begin a three-day [[general strike]] across the country to protest [[Prime Minister of Belgium|Prime Minister]] [[Bart de Wever]]'s government of "[[social disruption|social dismantling]]" through budget cuts in their savings program. [https://www.dw.com/en/belgium-faces-nationwide-disruption-as-unions-strike/a-74870459 (DW)]
